line: Life springs from sorrow and calamity, and death from ease and pleasure.
Ice crushed their ship. Six men sailed a small boat about 1,300 km for help. All 28 came home.
Heat and cold, sorrows and joys... Bear with it... As the wise bear.
Character cannot be developed in ease and quiet. Only through experiences of trial and suffering can the soul be strengthened.
credit: Helen Keller · Helen Keller's Journal (1938), p. 60

line: Without work, you can't even pull a little fish out of a pond.
credit: Russian proverb · recorded by Vladimir Dal

line: A sword's sharp edge comes from grinding. The plum blossom's scent comes from bitter cold.
Fire tests gold, misfortune brave men.
credit: Seneca, On Providence 5.10 · tr. John W. Basore

line: What is needed is constant work, day and night, constant reading, study, will.
credit: Anton Chekhov, letter to his brother, 1886 · tr. Constance Garnett

line: Tenzing Norgay went to Everest six times. On the seventh, in 1953, he and Hillary reached the top.

credit: Japanese proverb · 艱難汝を玉にす
